## v83 same-model negated comparison rescue experiment (2026-09-21)

Using the ready v9 / quality-v2 local server, four matched MADLAD greedy requests tested syntax alternatives for the exact group-comparison failure. The original sentence with `..., compared to those who reported not to have looked...` reproduced the negation reversal even when sent alone. A syntax-equivalent two-sentence variant translated the two groups correctly and retained both means, SDs, U and p. A same-sentence `whereas` variant dropped the lower-score contrast. Reversing the group order into a “negative group had lower scores, whereas the positive group had higher scores” sentence produced a meaning-faithful translation and passed the current client quality checks. Full inputs/outputs are in ignored `test-data/real-papers/reports/translation-audit-v83-negated-comparison-segmentation.json`.

This identifies a promising structure-sensitive rescue candidate; it does not yet justify a production source rewrite. Reconstructing comparative syntax automatically can itself alter scope, so expand positive and negative controls across several independent papers before coding a generic transformer. Do not count the manually reformulated candidate as a successful production translation or as fallback-rate improvement.

Before the change, the app's custom reassignment masked this upstream bug in its active 5.16.1 environment; it is now replaced by fail-closed integrity checks and a 4.57.6 pin (including protobuf for the slow T5 tokenizer). Full reproducible method and fixture outputs: [TRANSFORMERS_MADLAD_AB.md](TRANSFORMERS_MADLAD_AB.md).

Correctly loaded 4.57.6 still reproduces MADLAD semantic drift: it narrows “none of the groups” to two groups and mis-scopes the 88 participant total; the existing client scope gate rejects those fixtures. Dense statistics were preserved. The same ten-paper / 40-unit extraction and reader-path cohort was rerun under 4.57.6: 18 pre-model plus 5 post-model fallbacks, 17 accepted translations; clean ordinary-body fallback remains 4/17 (23.5%), unchanged from patched 5.x. Twelve generated outputs differed; manual review found material false accepts on factory-worker study focus, interactive jewellery overview, consumer-production terminology, and WEAR construct claims. Runtime repair is confirmed, product quality goals remain unmet. ## v47 decode-path isolation (diagnostic only)

Replayed the two v46 severity-2 false accepts through production `/translate` on one loaded MADLAD process with `TRANSLATION_UNIT_DEBUG=1`; exact inputs/outputs and chunk/decode trace are in `/tmp/paper-reader-semantic-v47.log`, with replay JSON in `/tmp/paper-reader-semantic-v47-replay.json`. Both errors reproduced without fallback. The 827-character participant paragraph sent the intact 161-character sentence “Eighty-eight participants from various fields of study ...”; greedy decode itself produced `各学科から88名...`, incorrectly suggesting 88 per field. All numeric facts survived, so the current numeric invariant scored it as acceptable.

The statistical block's first sentence was a 340-character chunk. Citation/statistic protection replaced `(H(2)=4.17, p=0.124)` and another stats group with opaque placeholders; greedy and beam outputs both translated “None of the groups...” as `両群間...`. The complete response later correctly stated that there were three study groups, but no block-level consistency guard caught the contradiction. Replaying that sentence alone and with “The study compared three groups...” in the same request reproduced `両群間`; therefore segmentation, batching, and postprocessing are not the first point of corruption. The model decode emits the semantic shift, while the quality gate false-accepts it because it checks number/negation preservation but not collective cardinality.

Eight same-process variants are saved at `/tmp/paper-reader-semantic-v47-variants.json` (token counts included). Rephrasing to “No significant differences were found among the three groups...” yielded a correct `3群間...` output (31 input / 17 output tokens); explicitly adding “three” to the original “None of the ...” construction also fixed that isolated case, but adding a later three-group context did not fix the first sentence. Participant-count variants remained unstable: one reordered variant omitted 88 and 5€ despite no fallback, while “88 participants overall ... across multiple fields” preserved 88 but phrased field scope ambiguously. These are diagnostic examples, not evidence that source rewriting is safe.

No production algorithm was changed in v47. Root attribution: primary MADLAD decode; secondary quality gate (false accept). Citation protection may contribute by hiding context, but it is not sufficient to explain the wrong “both groups” reading because the original sentence alone reproduces it. Next: build held-out cross-domain tests for collective quantifier/cardinality and participant-count scope, evaluate a general semantic verification/cascade signal with false-reject accounting, and do not deploy a brittle phrase rewrite or blacklist. Then expand manual review beyond the three-paper cohort. Debug artifacts are temporary under `/tmp`; no benchmark is running. The debug process has been stopped and normal PID 83146 is ready: `/health` reports `model_loaded=true`, `phase=ready`, and `/status` confirms the same model version. Startup logs show warmup `OK` rejected for lacking Japanese script, but model startup completes and health is ready; this is an existing warmup-validation quirk, not a server readiness failure.

On the cognitive VR paper, native geometry showed two generic layout failures: sparse body lines on a page with large figures hid a two-column layout, and a left publication/date rail shared baselines with the main text. `pdfLayout.ts` now detects sparse paired column origins, prevents a narrow rail from merging into wide body lines, reattaches a short statistical continuation to its caption, and stitches high-confidence same-column/cross-page continuation fragments. It also carries only the unfinished prefix across a column boundary, preserving the unrelated remainder.

Fresh v42 reader-path run `test-data/real-papers/reports/translation-audit-v42-margin-stitch.json`: 12 rows, 6 accepted / 6 visible source fallbacks. Accepted model translations averaged 8.13 seconds each in this run; this is descriptive, not a controlled speed comparison.

The cross-page reconstruction removes the prior incomplete input ending `... by comparing`; the formerly hallucinated “10 vs 20 cases” output is no longer produced. - Figure 5 caption continues on the next native text line: first line ends `Significant`, next begins `differences between groups are marked...`. The extraction block contains only the first line because same-page paragraph formation missed the continuation. Primary cause: paragraph reconstruction / block grouping. Next: inspect neighboring canonical/layout candidates and add a generic caption-continuation test.

## Architecture（現行）

- **シェル**: Tauri 2 macOS。UI は React。翻訳サイドカーはアプリが spawn / 終了時に停止
- **本文の正本**: Paper Package（`<AppData>/papers/<paperId>/`）— [DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md](./DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **索引・所属・メモ・読書位置・用語・FTS**: SQLite `library.sqlite`（schema v6: `needs_translation_resume`）
- **Reader open**: document / layout / source.pdf / assets を分離。既定 load は markdown + structure のみ。図は `assets/…` パスを保持し必要時に Blob 化
- **document cache**: `dirty` フラグ。read-only open → close では package を再 write しない
- **FTS**: annotation CRUD と translation checkpoint で per-paper incremental refresh
- **ReaderScreen**: hooks に分割（document / glossary / search / annotations / export / translation resume / reading position）。挙動は維持
- **抽出**: `extractAcademicPdf` → CanonicalDocument → Package。詳細は [ACADEMIC_PDF_EXTRACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md](./ACADEMIC_PDF_EXTRACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **翻訳**: MADLAD-400 3B / MPS / bf16、文バッチ既定 24、品質ゲート（pipeline v71 / strict-restore-v16）。監査手順は [TRANSLATION_CORPUS_AUDIT.md](./TRANSLATION_CORPUS_AUDIT.md)
- **硬化メモ**: [P0_HARDENING.md](./P0_HARDENING.md)
- **packaged acceptance**: [docs/RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md](./docs/RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md)

## Known limitations / 残課題

### 2026-09-18 pending-PDF extraction probe

- 翻訳 server は `127.0.0.1:8765` で応答していないため、v12 の fresh translation benchmark はまだ再実行していない。
- 保留PDF 2件を現行抽出へ通し、`test-data/real-papers/reports/pending-extraction-probe-v1.json` に固定した。`human-ai-interaction-guidelines.pdf` は8ページ/153 blocks、`covid-ml-review.pdf` は17ページ/225 blocks。
- この診断で、一般化可能な抽出残差を確認した。Human-AI paper の page 1 では図ラベル由来の短い候補が `title`/`author`/`affiliation` と競合し、本文タイトル以外に `"'s Emphasis of Human-AI Interaction Guidelines"` が title になっている。COVID review では abstract の複数行が affiliation と分類され、タイトルも `"Diagnosis ...: A"` と `"Review"` に分割されている。
- いずれも文字列ブラックリストや論文固有条件は追加していない。次は native geometry/style、candidate evidence、resolver のどの層で誤昇格したかを診断し、production変更前に synthetic/real-paper regressionを追加する。翻訳品質の数値は server 復旧後に取得する。
- 診断後の汎用修正として、短いタイトル継続行を段組み境界をまたいで結合し、先頭が possessive fragment になる単一native spanをベクター図ラベル evidence として `other` へ競合させる処理を追加。COVID reviewは `Diagnosis ...: A Review` に結合され、Human-AIの図タイトル断片はcanonical title候補から除外された。診断結果は `test-data/real-papers/reports/pending-title-geometry-v3.json` に保存。
- 修正後に `npm run typecheck`、`npm run lint -- --deny-warnings`、`npm run test:extraction-corpus -- --run` を実行し、real-paper extraction/reading-order **76/76 passed**。翻訳 serverは未起動で、fresh v12翻訳指標は未更新。
- possessive vector-figure fragment の synthetic regression を `src/test/pdfExtraction/pipeline.test.ts` に追加し、focused pipeline **25/25 passed**。`generateGenericCandidates` が `vector-figure-label-cluster` evidence を出し、`other` 競合を保持することを固定した。
- masthead直下に`Abstract`見出しがないPDFで、長い折返し英文を`affiliation`へ誤分類しない一般条件を追加。COVID reviewのabstract先頭〜中盤の長文行がparagraphへ戻ることを実PDFで確認した（短い残片は引き続き要調査）。変更後もextraction corpus **76/76 passed**、typecheck/lint成功。
- 追加のnative geometry診断で、残りの短い`and detecting...`/`applying...`は段組み再配置で幅の狭い小文字継続行になっていたと確認。小文字・接続詞開始かつ機関名/メールでない行を本文継続として扱い、これらもparagraphへ戻した。extraction corpus **76/76 passed**。
- 現行ツリーで全Vitest **63 files / 385 tests passed**。translation-server単体回帰も `PYTHONPATH=translation-server ... unittest discover` で **119 tests passed**。最初のPython実行はPYTHONPATH不足でimport errorになったが、コード不具合ではなく環境変数を付けて再実行し成功した。localhost server・fresh translation benchmarkは未起動。
- localhost停止中でも監査値を再集計し、`test-data/real-papers/audit-metrics.json` を更新。レビュー済み58/80件の暫定値は ordinary-body 36件で post-model fallback 8/36 = **22.2%**、semantic error 4/36 = **11.1%**、unsafe false-accept **46.4%**（accepted 28件中 severity>=2 が13件）。これは未レビュー22件を含まない暫定値で、目標の5%以下・安全水準には未到達。自動acceptを正解扱いせず、サーバー復旧後のv12 fresh benchmarkと追加手動レビューを優先する。
- accepted 重大レビュー行を現行品質ゲートへ再評価する診断 `scripts/audit-translation-relation-signals.ts` を追加し、`test-data/real-papers/reports/semantic-relation-gate-audit-v1.json` を生成。17件中13件に関係信号（否定・比較・因果・条件・時間）があり、6件は原文信号が出力側で検出できないにもかかわらず、現行ゲートが score 1.0・理由なしでacceptした。これは自動rejectの根拠ではなく、semantic false-acceptを測定し selective cascade / claim-alignmentへ接続するための診断である。単純な日本語キーワード一致は十分な意味判定ではないため、次はこの6件と正常例で精度を校正してからproduction gateへの影響を検討する。
- 既存の代替モデル成果物を再確認した。`selective-cascade-audit-v2.json` は12候補中 conservative eligible 0、`selective-cascade-decision-v1.json` は no production cascade、`selective-cascade-simulation-v1.json` も blind manual semantic label 未検証のため出荷不可としている。M2M100 1.2B/418M と Opus の ordinary 比較には、反復・語順崩壊・固有語誤訳が残り、現MADLADの代替として採用できる証拠はない。単一モデル切替はせず、fresh benchmark 復旧後に同一fixtureで再評価する。
- 関係信号の欠落6件を原文・訳文で手動再確認し、`semantic-relation-manual-review-v1.json` に保存。4件は日本語の自然な談話順序で補われるため信号false-positive、2件は用語・文書内参照の実質的な意味損失を含む。単純な信号欠落をhard rejectにせず、構造参照と用語整合のblind校正へ分離する方針を確定した。
- `quality.ts` の `unsafeParagraphStructureReason` に、文末が `Section`/`Figure`/`Table`/`Appendix`/`Chapter` だけで終わる未完了の文書内参照を検出する一般条件を追加。後続ブロックと結合できない場合にモデルの番号推測・参照欠落を防ぐ。`src/test/quality.test.ts` に回帰を追加し、quality **68/68**、typecheck、lint、diff-checkが成功。これはsource fallbackを増やすだけの最終策ではなく、上流stitchで修復できない残片を安全に扱うための境界条件である。
- 既存manual-review 80行への影響を調査し、この条件に一致したのは2行だけ。いずれも実際に文末が`Section`で途切れたsource fragment（1件は既存pre-model fallback、1件は誤ってacceptされたseverity 2）で、通常の完全文は巻き込まれていない。
- 変更後に全Vitest **63 files / 385 tests passed**。PDF.jsのcanvas polyfill警告のみで、翻訳モデル・サーバー・`.app`は起動／変更していない。
- `ScientificInvariant` に番号付き `Section`/`Chapter`/`Appendix` の `structure` kind を追加。表記が「第3節」のようにローカライズされても元の参照番号を検証し、欠落や別番号を品質ゲートで拒否する。`quality.test.ts` は **69/69**、typecheck、lint、diff-check成功。一般数値や図表本文は対象外。
- この品質ゲート変更に合わせ、client/serverの `MADLAD_MODEL_VERSION` を `3b-mt-v5-semantic-v71-strict-restore-v15` へ更新。v12以前の翻訳キャッシュを再利用せず、構造参照検査を通した結果だけを採用する。モデル重み・生成設定は変更していない。
- 抽出側の `isSentenceContinuation` に、`... in Section` → `3` のような文書内参照ラベルと直後の番号を結合する一般条件を追加。全Vitest **63 files / 386 tests passed**、typecheck、lint、diff-check成功。抽出単位が変わるためclient/serverのcache versionをv16へ更新した。
- `titleResolver` に、タイトル候補の後ろへ混入したORCID/URL/メールをmasthead suffixとして切り離す一般条件を追加。曖昧な著者名推測は行わず、明確な連絡先トークンだけを境界にする。v16で新しい抽出結果を再評価する。
- v15後のreal-paper extraction corpusを長時間セッションで完走し、reading-order 37 + baseline 39 の **76/76 passed**。PDF.jsのcanvas/フォント/TT警告のみで、参照結合修正による抽出回帰は確認されなかった。

## Release readiness

### Pause checkpoint (2026-09-15)

Corpus-audit work is paused at a clean boundary. No benchmark, test, or audit
job is running. The packaged app translation server remains running because it
belongs to the user's launched `.app`; it was left untouched.

Resume from Phase 1 attribution of the 15 remaining ordinary-body fallbacks.
The measured rate is still 15/74 (20.27%), so the <=5% goal is not met. Next,
capture canonical block geometry and `TRANSLATION_UNIT_DEBUG=1` traces for all
15 rows before adding new rules.

### Phase 1 attribution evidence (2026-09-15)

Added `scripts/attribute-translation-fallbacks.ts` and generated
`test-data/real-papers/reports/translation-fallback-attribution.json` without
starting the translation server. All 15 remaining fallback rows matched
exactly one extracted Canonical block and one layout block, so page/bbox
evidence is now available. Preliminary cause hypotheses are A model/adequacy
9, D structure mixing 3, and E scientific layout 3. No matched fallback block
currently shows a within-block column switch, so reading-order failure has not
been claimed from this evidence. These
labels are explicitly hypotheses until manual line-level review; no production
heuristic was changed from this inventory.

The fixed fixture was rerun under `3b-mt-v5-semantic-v61`; direct, micro-batch,
protection, atomic citation, whole-sentence, and repeat outputs were
deterministic. No unrelated hallucinated fact appeared, while terminology
remains awkward (for example 「移動領域」), confirming a semantic adequacy
issue rather than a splitter or batch failure.

Segmenter v62 now merges leading two- or three-word prefixes forward (while
preserving colon-ended list lead-ins). This addresses meaningless first units
seen in several source-echo paragraphs; cache identity is `semantic-v62`.
Segmenter tests pass, but full-corpus impact is not yet measured.

Added a source-grounded terminology repair for `mobile domain` → `モバイル分野`
when the model emits `移動領域`; unrelated sources are untouched. Glossary
tests (16) and TypeScript validation pass. Full-corpus fallback impact remains
unmeasured until the next benchmark.

The line-level source-integrity pass found 14/15 matched blocks with one
consistent column, no list boundary, and no continuation edge. One block
(`cognitive-psychology-gpt3/b-b4ed26af`) contains four detected list lines and
is marked `review`; it remains a structure-mixing candidate rather than a
model-only failure.

The existing fixed-fixture model isolation report shows direct and
MicroBatchScheduler parity (64 input / 86 output tokens), parity with and
without production protection, and deterministic greedy output. Atomic
author-year citation protection preserves the full citation and the safe
two-chunk split remains coherent. No unrelated hallucinated fact appears in
this isolated sentence, so semicolon splitting and batch mapping are not
supported as its direct cause.

### Qwen 2.5 3B audit smoke (2026-09-15)

Downloaded `qwen2.5:3b` via Ollama for audit-only local/free evaluation. Three deterministic smoke cases were saved in `test-data/real-papers/reports/model-quality-qwen2.5-3b-smoke-v1.json`. It correctly preserved the author-year citation group and the `2013` sentence boundary, but the scientific sentence output contained the Chinese character `显著` in otherwise Japanese text. The model is therefore promising for citation-heavy prose but not production-ready without a language-quality gate and broader held-out review. No production routing or packaged app files were changed.

Qwen 2.5 3B 12-row fixture evaluation completed (audit-only, deterministic temperature 0, `num_predict=512`) and saved at `test-data/real-papers/reports/model-quality-qwen2.5-3b-v1.json`. It completed all 12 rows with latency roughly 0.9–7.3s each, but outputs frequently retained English fragments (`perspective`, `reflection`, `curve`, `context`, `computer`) and one row included the unrelated term `患者`. This is evidence that Qwen cannot be blindly cascaded; a broader manual claim review and a language/terminology gate are required before any routing change.

Added an audit-only mixed-script signal to `translation-server/scripts/score_candidate_selection.py`: simplified-Chinese-only CJK characters are reported as `mixedScriptRisk` without changing production acceptance or routing. A regression test covers the Qwen smoke failure (`显著`), and the candidate-selection test suite passes (4 tests).

The candidate-selection harness now accepts both `results` and `rows` report schemas. Running it against the 12-row Qwen fixture produced 12 candidates and 11/12 surface hard-signal passes. This high pass rate despite observed English fragments/unrelated terminology confirms these signals are insufficient for automatic routing; the report remains audit-only.

Qwen prompt-variant smoke (same scientific sentence, temperature 0) was completed in `model-quality-qwen2.5-3b-prompt-smoke-v1.json`. Three prompts, including an explicit Japanese-only instruction, all deterministically emitted `显著`; prompt wording does not explain the mixed-script failure. This is model-output behavior and should be handled by candidate quality gating or excluded routing, not prompt-only changes.

Qwen 2.5 7B smoke completed after local download (`model-quality-qwen2.5-7b-smoke-v1.json`). It translated the p-value sentence and citation-heavy sentence cleanly, but the year-boundary sentence switched to Chinese (`我们的发现对于研究人员具有价值`) and retained English. This is better than 3B on citation prose but still fails language consistency; it remains audit-only pending held-out semantic review and a robust language gate.

A preliminary manual label file for the 7B smoke is recorded at `model-quality-qwen2.5-7b-smoke-manual-v1.json`: 1 correct, 1 minor wording, 1 severity-3 reject. This is only a three-case smoke and is not a production quality estimate.

Qwen 2.5 7B full 12-row fixture evaluation completed (`model-quality-qwen2.5-7b-v1.json`). Mean latency was 7.4s/row (range 1.7–16.0s). Compared with 3B, 7B produced substantially more coherent Japanese and preserved the OzCHI citation row, but several long outputs retained English/uppercase terms and require semantic review. No simplified-Chinese drift was observed in this run, yet this is not sufficient evidence for automatic routing; manual claim labels and held-out validation remain required.

Manual claim review of all 12 Qwen 2.5 7B fixture outputs is now recorded in `model-quality-qwen2.5-7b-manual-v1.json`: 5 correct, 5 minor/terminology issues, 1 severity-3 hallucination (an unsupported political/economic conclusion), and 1 additional terminology issue. This confirms improved fluency does not guarantee semantic safety; Qwen remains audit-only.

Calibration correction: the mixed-script audit set was narrowed to characters absent from Japanese orthography; common shared kanji are no longer flagged. Re-running Qwen 7B selection gives `mixedScriptRisk=0` for that fixture (the known Chinese drift remains represented by the 3B report). This avoids a false-positive audit signal and production behavior remains unchanged.

Manual review of the Qwen 2.5 14B fixture is recorded in `model-quality-qwen2.5-14b-manual-v1.json`: 4 correct, 6 minor wording/terminology, 1 severity-2 omission, and 1 severity-3 language failure (a full Chinese output). Although 14B improves the citation and year-boundary smoke cases, its 12-row severe-error rate is 2/12 and latency averages ~15.5s/row; it is not safe for production cascade without stronger gating.

Qwen 14B selector calibration joined surface signals to the manual labels in `qwen14-selector-vs-manual-v1.json`: 11/12 passed hard surface signals, while 2/12 had manual severity >=2 and both passed those signals. Surface-only routing would therefore have a 18.2% unsafe false-accept rate on this fixture; no cascade is enabled.

Audit-only selective-cascade simulation for Qwen 14B (`selective-cascade-qwen14-oracle-v1.json`) joins its manual labels to the existing unsafe cohort. On the overlapping 12 rows, 10 would be rescued and 2 would remain fallback, with 0 severe selected rows—but this is oracle-style (labels were assigned after seeing outputs), so it cannot justify production routing. Held-out automatic semantic selection is still required.

Qwen 14B semantic-coverage audit (`semantic-coverage-qwen14-v1.json`) and threshold curves (`qwen14-semantic-calibration-v1.json`) are complete. A min-source similarity threshold of 0.70 retains 8/12 rows but still retains 1/2 manually severe rows (12.5% unsafe); thresholds do not reach the <=5% safety target. The embedding signal remains audit-only and is not promoted to production gating.

Post-Qwen audit verification: translation-server unittest discovery passes 98 tests (including the mixed-script and rows-schema changes), `git diff --check` passes, and the user-launched bundled server PID 60582 remains healthy (`/health` ready, model_loaded=true).

Local-model manual comparison (`local-model-manual-comparison-v1.json`) now consolidates the same 12-row fixture. Qwen 14B prompt-rescue experiment (`model-quality-qwen2.5-14b-prompt-rescue-v1.json`) reran the previously severe thermal-earring row with three explicit Japanese-only prompts and `num_predict=512`. All three outputs were Japanese, preserved 11.3mm/31mm/335mg/14.4μW/28 days, and avoided the prior Chinese failure. This indicates prompt/template sensitivity for that row, but it is a single rescue experiment; Qwen remains audit-only until the same prompt is evaluated on held-out rows and semantic safety is measured.

Held-out prompt evaluation for Qwen 14B (`model-quality-qwen2.5-14b-heldout-prompt-v1.json`) completed on 3 ordinary blocks. The Japanese-only prompt improves language consistency but does not guarantee claim preservation, so Qwen remains audit-only.

Qwen14 held-out segmented rescue (`model-quality-qwen2.5-14b-heldout-segmented-v1.json`) split the previous 2-sentence block into two complete translation units. It supports validating sentence-level rescue segmentation before any model cascade, while production MADLAD routing remains unchanged.

Therefore the Qwen rescue experiment validates the segmentation path but does not justify another segmenter code change; remaining quality gap is model/candidate selection and extraction-specific unit construction.

### 2026-09-15 resume semantics and runtime interruption

Fixed benchmark `--resume` semantics: a checkpoint is skipped only when its row
count reaches the current `--limit`; partial checkpoints are retried. The retry
then encountered a socket close and the packaged server was no longer listening
(`/health` connection refused), so the audit remains partial and no server was
restarted by this session. TypeScript validation and the 106-test Python suite
still pass.

The audit client now bounds each translation request with
`MADLAD_BENCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 180s) and retries once after a
transient fetch/socket failure. This is benchmark reliability only; no reader
routing or server lifecycle behavior changed. TypeScript and diff checks pass.

A second resume fix preserves previously completed partial rows when a retry
fails: the report now retains the prior rows alongside the new error, while
only rows meeting the requested limit are skipped. `tsc --noEmit` and diff
checks pass. The current failed report had already been overwritten before this
fix, so its earlier two rows cannot be recovered from that file; future retries
will preserve them.

**Hypothesis:** orientation-aware clustering exposed the wear-scale correlation matrix, but its numeric rotated blocks still competed as ordinary paragraphs because generic table evidence (0.90) stayed below the resolver's precision threshold.

**Before:** page 14's 90° numeric grid was source-preserving but paragraph-shaped; rotated cells could still be sent through the paragraph projection.

**After:** sizeable numeric-rich rotated clusters receive stronger table evidence (0.97), allowing the existing Document Resolver to select `table` while ordinary aligned rows retain the conservative 0.90 score. Added a real-paper regression assertion for `wear-scale` page 14. Extraction corpus remains 42/42; TypeScript and lint pass.

**Safety:** the evidence requires at least 30 rotated native items and 30% numeric content, so isolated rotated labels/annotations remain paragraph fallback. The caption text is still interleaved (`Inter-item correlation matrix6Table`) and structured cell reconstruction remains open.

### Orientation-aware native text ordering (2026-09-16)

Rotated lines now join item text along the native text-matrix baseline rather than always sorting by horizontal x. This addresses rotated captions and cell labels whose PDF content stream order differs from visual order, while horizontal lines retain the previous x/y ordering. Reading-order 37/37, extraction corpus 42/42, typecheck, and diff checks pass. Further visual review is required before claiming caption recall improvement.

### Flattened native table geometry (2026-09-16)

The unresolved OzCHI Table 3/5 cases were traced to an early `cellLines.length === 0` return in the generic table evidence generator: grids emitted as one native item per line never reached the geometry test. A conservative flattened-grid evidence path now runs before that return and requires at least six lines, two repeated x-origin bands, compact line widths, punctuation-light text, and at most 40 words. The resolver applies the identical predicate for caption-adjacent region membership, so cells are not sent through paragraph projection. OzCHI table-region recall improved from 0.8 (4/5) to 1.0 (5/5); the 26-paper baseline source-integrity mean remains 1.0 and chrome contamination remains 0. Full extraction corpus (56 tests), full Vitest (61 files / 353 tests), and TypeScript validation pass. This remains a native-geometry rule with no paper-specific strings; broader benchmark review is still required before declaring extraction complete.

Follow-up verification (2026-09-16): reran the full 26-paper extraction baseline after flattened-grid detection. No paper remains below its expected table-region recall (all reported table recall values are 1.0), aggregate source integrity remains 1.0, and lint/typecheck pass. The new synthetic regression confirms a caption-adjacent two-band one-item grid produces a canonical table region without projecting its cells as translatable paragraph content.

### Table-region precision review (2026-09-16)

Manual canonical inspection of OzCHI page 8/9 found pre-existing false-positive table members: long paragraph fragments and a bullet introduction were admitted beside Table 5. The flattened-grid change itself was not the cause (the false positives reproduce without it). A resolver guard now identifies long prose and bullet-only streams and excludes them unless strong row geometry is present. Existing synthetic table, extraction corpus (56), and full Vitest (354) pass; further native table precision work is pending because some false positives still receive strong multi-item evidence.

### Multi-item ratio / prose precision guard (2026-09-16)

Manual canonical inspection showed that long column fragments with only one or two multi-item lines could be promoted as table candidates. Region membership now requires a repeated multi-item-line ratio for non-numeric candidates; bullet-only streams remain excluded. A candidate prose-shape guard (>20 words) prevents incomplete column fragments from receiving the strongest structural-grid score, while short real tables remain eligible. OzCHI inspection no longer promotes the previously observed long results paragraph or bullet introduction to table; the expected Table 1–5 nodes remain. Extraction corpus remains 56/56 and full Vitest 354/354.

### Table candidate prose-shape refinement (2026-09-16)

Manual OzCHI canonical review confirmed that incomplete multi-column prose (8+ lines, 20+ words) could receive structural-grid evidence because its first/last native lines had multiple items. The generic candidate guard now treats that shape as prose unless it is a true flattened grid; this removes the two observed prose candidates while preserving Table 1–5 and existing synthetic grids. Extraction corpus 56/56, full Vitest 354/354, lint, and typecheck pass. Remaining table rows without a caption are still intentionally conservative.

Verification correction (2026-09-16): the broad candidate prose-shape suppression reduced OzCHI table-region recall to 0.8 and was reverted. The resolver-side multi-item/bullet guards remain; canonical manual review still shows strong multi-item prose candidates requiring a safer geometry criterion.

### Structural-grid precision experiment (2026-09-16)

Tested requiring repeated x columns across at least three native lines for the strong structural-grid score. Existing extraction tests and OzCHI recall remained green, but the manually observed long prose candidates were produced by the separate `proseGrid` path and were unchanged. Reverted this no-benefit candidate change; next work should improve `proseGrid` using row-level geometry rather than broad word-count suppression.

A further geometry check requires proseGrid candidates to contain at least two distinct line-origin bands in addition to indented rows. This removes the page-8 results prose candidate in manual OzCHI inspection while preserving expected table regions and all extraction tests. A page-9 bullet/table-like stream remains under review because its native item geometry is more ambiguous.

## TableRegion boundary investigation (2026-09-16)

The first generic experiment (caption-index iteration) was reverted after diagnostic regeneration showed unreviewed additional regions (16 total), so it was not promoted. This preserves the reviewed 13-region baseline and avoids changing production heuristics without visual evidence. The remaining root-cause attribution is: the current caption-anchored signature uses one page-level first-caption window (420pt), allowing independent tables or surrounding graphics to fall within one candidate bbox. A follow-up fix must split signatures at independent caption/grid boundaries and use graphics/prose negative evidence, then visually review every changed region before adoption.

Because this changes the review surface beyond the original 13, it remains an experiment and is not production-approved; all new outputs require render review before adoption.

### 2026-09-20 scheduler panel-label false-fallback repair

- Root cause: `is_probable_panel_fragment()` classified every <=240-character unit beginning `(a)`–`(z)` as a panel fragment. `MicroBatchScheduler` then returned that whole source unit without invoking MADLAD. A complete English clause such as `(b) in some parts of the experiment, the decisions have consequences ...` therefore remained English, and the client correctly rejected the mixed-language paragraph.
- Generic fix: only a standalone `(a)`/`(b)` marker is now skipped; panel markers embedded at the start of captions are protected as atomic scientific spans, so the caption body goes through the existing translation/restore pipeline. Added tests for standalone markers, full-sentence captions, and preservation of panel labels.
- Verification: translation-server Python suite **121/121 passed**; `git diff --check` passed. Same-process, same-loaded-MADLAD replay on five panel-prefixed source-echo examples produced 4/5 scheduler translations without a source echo; the fifth (social-influence block) still source-fell back because a different clause failed phrase-repetition validation. Panel-prefixed prose is now present in actual MADLAD inputs. The medical example still demonstrates unrelated model errors (for example, 33.9°C decoded as 23.9°C and participant rendered as patient); this repair does not claim to resolve semantic decode quality.
- Diagnostic artifact overwritten with the focused 5-row replay at `test-data/real-papers/reports/source-echo-diagnosis-fresh-20260920-v16.json`. The complete 36-paper cohort was not rerun, so fallback-rate effect is not yet measured. Current 5% ordinary-body fallback target remains unmet. No benchmark server is running.

The 5.17.0 raw load maps the encoder embedding to `lm_head.weight` (absmax 2.14) while the decoder uses `decoder.embed_tokens.weight` (absmax 253), and `encoder_equals_decoder` is false. The 5.17.0 repaired run explicitly restores the encoder tensor and records the repair; production is already pinned to `transformers==4.57.6` in `translation-server/requirements.lock` and the server enforces that runtime version. Existing 4.57.6 server-pipeline outputs still reproduce several semantic failures, so the runtime-loading defect is real but does not explain all quality failures. No production dependency change was made. Artifacts: `madlad-transformers-5.17.0-raw.json`, `madlad-transformers-5.17.0-ab.json`, `madlad-transformers-4.57.6-ab.json`, `madlad-transformers-4.57.6-server-pipeline.json`.

## 2026-09-22 model-suffix invariant false-positive fix

The remaining Power-over-Skin ordinary-body fallback was traced to the quality gate, not translation semantics: Japanese compaction `AirPods Pro 2` → `AirPodsPro2` caused the attached `2` to be classified as an unexpected citation and the source acronym `AirPods` to appear missing. Scientific invariant extraction now ignores digits attached to mixed-case identifiers as citation candidates, and output matching accepts a compact mixed-case model identifier only when the source contains the corresponding acronym + descriptor + numeric suffix pattern. Added a regression test. Quality tests pass 121/121, typecheck and lint pass. Fresh live replay `post-model-suffix-gate-power-v1.{json,md}` now shows 7/7 ordinary-body rows accepted (0 fallback); damaged-extraction rows remain correctly excluded.

## 2026-09-22 compact section-reference invariant normalization

A held-out row (`thermal-earring:b-a0365a0b`) had a faithful output `5.2で説明しました` rejected because the source used `Section 5.2`. The structural invariant matcher now accepts a bare Japanese section number only when it is immediately used with an explicit reference verb (`で説明`, `に示`, `において`, or `を参照`); a bare number remains rejected. The stored source/output now scores cleanly offline (`score: 1`, no reasons). Added positive and negative regression tests; quality suite passes 123/123, typecheck and lint pass. A live replay remains needed to update the production report.

## 2026-09-22 SI-unit spacing invariant normalization

The held-out `step-to-charge` row exposed a generic PDF extraction artifact: `1MHz` was extracted as `1M Hz`, so a faithful Japanese output was flagged as an unexpected measurement. Scientific invariant extraction now recognizes SI-prefix spacing (`1M Hz`) as the same measurement family as the compact form, while preserving exact numeric values and leaving missing acronyms/statistics as real failures. Added regression coverage for `1M Hz` → `1MHz` and for an incorrect numeric value. Quality tests pass 124/124; typecheck and lint pass. No translation server or benchmark process is running.

## Transformers loading bug A/B — decisive result (2026-09-22)

- Ran the existing five-fixture diagnostic in isolated Transformers **5.17.0** and production Transformers **4.57.6**, same checkpoint/tokenizer, MPS, bfloat16, greedy generation, and fixture inputs.
- 5.17.0 loaded `encoder.embed_tokens` equal to `lm_head.weight` (absmax 2.140625) while decoder matched the decoder embedding (absmax 253). All five fixtures produced visibly broken output (Thai/Latin repetition, degenerate characters, or missing EOS).
- 4.57.6 loaded encoder and decoder equal to the checkpoint decoder embedding (absmax 253), with a separate lm_head (absmax 2.14). The same five fixtures produced Japanese output and reached EOS.
- This isolates the current semantic failures to the Transformers 5.x MADLAD loading bug; the failure is present at decode time, before PDF extraction, microbatch mapping, or postprocessing.
- Production is restored and healthy on `3b-mt-v6-transformers-4.57.6-semantic-v76-source-protect-v15-strict-restore-v28-quality-v10` (`model_loaded=true`, `phase=ready`).
- Artifacts: `translation-server/benchmarks/transformers-5.17.0-diagnosis.json`, `transformers-4.57.6-diagnosis.json`, and `transformers-madlad-loading-diagnostic-v1.md`.
- No production code or dependency change was needed because the lockfile already pins the safe 4.57.6 runtime.

## Scientific invariant hardening — Unicode mathematical units (2026-09-22)

- Root cause found in PPG `b-93499466`: source units used mathematical italic Unicode (`𝑚𝑚`, `𝑢𝑊`), so the invariant extractor failed to register `1.49 mm`; a translation corrupting it to `1.49ml×1.49ni` incorrectly passed quality 1.0.
- Generic fix: normalize source and invariant values with Unicode NFKC before measurement matching/comparison. No paper-specific term or hallucination blacklist was added.
- Added regression test for mathematical italic units. Quality/model-version tests: **132/132**, typecheck passed, translation-server tests: **173/173**, `git diff --check` passed.

## Scientific acronym boundary fix (2026-09-22)

- Fixed a generic false missing-invariant result for ASCII acronyms adjacent to Japanese text (`I2Cライン`, `BERTについて`). The previous comparison reused whitespace-stripped/unit-normalized values, which could turn `I2C` into a Celsius-like form and could merge `STW VIDI` into one synthetic token.
- Acronym matching now uses NFKC + case folding while preserving whitespace and treats only adjacent ASCII letters/digits as identifier boundaries. This preserves safety against substring matches without rejecting normal Japanese typography.
- Added regression coverage for `I2Cバス`; quality/model-version tests now pass **134/134**.
- Qwen b-934 rescue candidate now scores `accept=true`, quality `1.00`, with dimensions, power, Celsius, and `I2C` invariants preserved. This remains audit evidence only; Qwen cascade is not enabled.
- Typecheck passed; translation-server Python suite passed **176 tests + 11 subtests**; `git diff --check` passed.

## Sidebar merge attribution (2026-09-22)

## Continuation merge trace (2026-09-22)

- Direct trace confirms the merge loop processes `Pathology` with the preceding wide body block as its target, then processes the next body line with the previous body target and `Pathology` as a skipped block. This explains why a naive margin guard either contaminates the body or prevents legitimate body continuation.
- Temporary trace and all unsuccessful guards were removed. The remaining implementation task is to make the merge decision direction-aware: never merge a narrow margin block into a body target, while allowing the following body block to rejoin the original body target across that margin block.

## v308 cascade safety-regex repair (2026-09-23)

CAT関連は対象外として、翻訳品質改善を継続。`src/services/translation/quality.ts` の `isCascadeQualityAcceptable` にある危険理由フィルタを点検したところ、単語境界が正規表現の `\\b` ではなく実文字 U+0008 (backspace) になっており、一般的な `invariant` / `missing` / `untranslated` / `malformed` 等の理由をこの補助フィルタが検出できない状態だった。専用の関係理由リストは動作していたが、理由の追加時に安全側へ倒れない欠陥だったため、正規表現のエスケープを修正した。モデル、抽出器、fallback閾値は変更していない。

検証: `npm run typecheck` passed。focused Vitest 3 files / 155 tests passed (`quality.test.ts` 149, `ollamaTranslationEngine.test.ts` 5, `translationModelVersion.test.ts` 1)。PDF.jsの任意canvas.node警告は既存環境由来。v293 fresh auditのordinary-body fallbackは67/244 (27.46%)で、<=5%目標は未達。次は修正後のcascade候補に対する held-out評価と、fallback原因のうち protected-token restore / model quality rejectionを分離して一般化可能な改善を進める。

The v293 ordinary-body fallback attribution was saved as `test-data/real-papers/reports/translation-audit-v308-ordinary-fallback-attribution.json`: among 67 reader-visible fallbacks / 244 ordinary-body rows, 56 were quality/model rejection, 8 involved protected-token restoration, and 3 were pre-model extraction/structure skips. This is an attribution of the existing v293 report, not a new benchmark and not evidence that fallback quality is solved. It directs the next work toward model-output rescue and protection robustness while preserving the extraction safety boundary.

A `--resume` invocation on 2026-09-23 regenerated the generic `translation-audit.json` from checkpoints (`selected=52`, `skipping 51 checkpointed papers`); it did not provide a fresh post-v308 model comparison, so its 70/244 ordinary fallback count is intentionally not used as evidence. The fixed-cohort v293 attribution remains the authoritative baseline until a non-resumed run is completed.

## v339 structural-rescue benchmark completed (2026-09-23)

The fresh cached-only benchmark `test-data/real-papers/reports/translation-audit-v339-structural-rescue.json` completed normally: 51 papers / 408 rows, including 171 ordinary-body prose rows. 44 ordinary-body rows were reader-visible fallbacks (25.73%), so the <=5% target remains unmet. ## v340 exclusivity gate hardening (2026-09-23)

The Gemma probe exposed a real omission path: a source claim with `not only ... but also ...` was rendered without the second causal relation, while the existing `isPlausibleJaTranslation` still accepted it because `exclusivity relation missing` was only used by the cascade helper. The general quality gate now rejects that reason as well; positive/negative regression assertions were added. This intentionally prioritizes semantic safety and does not claim a fallback-rate improvement yet. Focused quality tests: 152/152; typecheck and lint pass.

## Bare superscript citation protection (2026-09-23)
Root cause confirmed for the HFE row: `protect_citations` did not protect single bare PDF superscript references such as `coaching29`, `review28`, `tool,31`, `EHR)30`, and `infection.30`; only the later client invariant gate detected their omission. Added a narrow generic `INLINE_BARE_REFERENCE_RE` with decimal and common identifier safeguards, plus round-trip regression coverage. The HFE source now protects numeric references `27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 24` before MADLAD. Python citation/quality tests: 107 passed (3 subtests). ## Protection A/B diagnostic checkpoint (2026-09-24)

The source-protection experiment has been implemented as a diagnostic-only benchmark in `translation-server/scripts/benchmark_protection_ab.py`. It compares raw, minimal, and current protection on the same extracted ordinary-body units, with optional production rescue, while keeping the loaded MADLAD 3B runtime and greedy decode fixed. The segmented 30-unit run (`protection-ab-diagnostic-v6-segmented-30.json`) completed all raw rows; minimal/current each had 2 strict restore failures. The matched production-rescue run (`protection-ab-diagnostic-v7-segmented-rescue-30.json`) completed all 30 current-path rows. These are engine/gate outcomes, not semantic correctness.

An additional 5-unit held-out production-rescue probe (`protection-ab-v8-heldout-5.json`) completed all five units on the verified 4.57.6 runtime; one identifier-only retry was exercised and no request ended in fallback. Outputs still require source-to-output semantic review, so this is coverage evidence only, not a quality-rate claim.

The earlier unsegmented 30-row report showed raw 22/30 engine errors versus minimal/current 23/30, but it included malformed/short units and is not a product-quality estimate. The segmented run is the valid comparison cohort. Existing paired outputs show both protection benefits (citations/statistical identifiers preserved) and costs (opaque spans can trigger strict fallback); no production protection reduction is justified yet. Keep current protection and strict restore enabled until blind semantic review of the paired raw/minimal/current outputs is complete. Python quality tests are 43/43 and `git diff --check` passes.

Provisional analyst review of 10 paired rows (`protection-ab-manual-review-v1.json`) found severity >=2 in 7/10. Three rows show a protection benefit (preserved RT+CT relation, citation/figure structure), three show MADLAD decode errors independent of protection, and three show protection-induced fallback or loss of context. This review is explicitly not blind and is not a production rate estimate. It supports a selective strategy: retain protection for opaque identifiers/citations, but evaluate context-preserving or alternate-model rescue for protected-span failures rather than globally removing placeholders. Verification after this checkpoint: frontend **67 files / 512 tests**, Python **43/43**, and `git diff --check` pass.

The v9 held-out probe exposed a generic unsafe case: a multi-measurement sentence retained all values but scrambled their order and attachment (`11.3 mm`, `31 mm`, `335 mg`, `14.4 uW`). Added `measurementOrderChanged()` to the quality evaluator. It only activates for three or more unit-bearing measurements, requires all source values to be present, and rejects a reordered sequence; one/two-measurement prose is unchanged. The real v9 output now scores 0.2828 with `scientific measurement order changed` instead of passing. Added positive and negative tests. Translation cache identity bumped from `quality-v21` to `quality-v22` so prior accepted outputs are not reused. Full frontend suite: **67 files / 514 tests**; typecheck/lint and diff check pass. This is a safety correction, not a fallback-rate improvement claim.

## v184 mixed-script semantic fragment guard (2026-09-24)

The PPG held-out model comparison exposed `光干渉metry`, a lowercase English decoder fragment attached to Japanese. The Qwen candidate output is now rejected for `untranslated mixed-script lexeme`; the existing PPG and measurement-order regressions remain caught. ## v189 protection-bearing delta analysis (2026-09-24)

Analyzed the 30-unit segmented raw/minimal/current artifact. Eleven units contained protected spans. Two units translated successfully in raw MADLAD but failed only under minimal/current strict restore because the model dropped a protected placeholder (`17 (Hospital, see SI Appendix)` and `VR`). The delta artifact is `reports/protection-ab-delta-v1.json`. This is direct evidence that opaque placeholder protection can add reader-visible fallback even when raw MADLAD completes; it is not evidence that removing protection is safe, because the same cohort also contains protection benefits and semantic decode errors. The next change should be a selective context-preserving rescue for dropped placeholders, with post-translation invariant verification, rather than global protection removal.
## v190 selective placeholder rescue implementation (2026-09-24)

Implemented a narrow server-side rescue for protected-span drops. After coordinated-clause rescue fails, the engine may retry only when every missing span is a plain identifier or a compact structural reference, including a generic numbered supplementary reference such as `17 (…see SI Appendix)`. Scientific equations, p-values, arbitrary prose, and unknown identifiers remain protected and still fail closed. This specifically addresses the two raw-success/current-fallback delta cases without globally disabling protection. Python quality tests now pass **44/44**, `py_compile` and `git diff --check` pass. The running server must be restarted before this code is active; no app bundle was built.

## v203 cascade false-reject diagnosis (2026-09-24)

The Qwen14 `step-to-charge:b-43efb21d` output was semantically plausible and passed `evaluateJaTranslation` with score 1 and no reasons, but `isCascadeQualityAcceptable` rejected it. Root cause was `hasCascadeSentenceCompression`: its raw period count treated `Eqn. 20` and `Fig. 2` labels as sentence boundaries, inflating the source count to 11 while the source actually contains six sentences. Replaced that count with a discourse-boundary split that requires a period to be followed by an uppercase sentence start, while preserving `!/?` boundaries. Added a regression test and bumped the quality identity to `quality-v28`. Focused quality tests pass; this is a targeted false-reject reduction, not evidence that Qwen is ready for production cascade.

## v253 protection A/B/C diagnostic (2026-09-24)

Ran `translation-server/scripts/benchmark_protection_ab.py` on 6 clean ordinary-body rows from multiple papers using one loaded MADLAD 3B process, identical greedy decoding, and raw/minimal/current protection arms. Artifact: `test-data/real-papers/reports/protection-ab-v253-6.json`. All three arms produced Japanese on 5/6 rows; the long measurement row failed in minimal/current because protected spans were dropped, while raw completed with severe numeric/unit drift. A short TRT/RT+CT abstract preserved the source acronym in raw but became `RTz+CTz` under minimal/current, showing that opaque protection can alter nearby context. Current protection also changed some name transliterations but preserved protected surface spans; raw did not provide reliable fact preservation. This small diagnostic does not justify production policy change: it supports reducing opaque spans selectively and relying on post-translation invariant verification, while retaining protection for high-risk identifiers/citations. The new malformed-placeholder rescue was active in the server benchmark v253 run, but remaining fallbacks include invariant and quality-gate failures. Next: expand the same-condition A/B to a stratified held-out sample and quantify protection benefit/cost before changing production routing.

## v603 selective cascade rejection diagnostics (2026-09-26)

Added `AlternateTranslationQualityError` diagnostics so the selective-cascade audit preserves alternate raw output and `TranslationQuality` when rescue is rejected. ## v604 condition relation false-reject reduction (2026-09-26)

The v603 alternate output for `thermal-earring:b-327fbccb` was semantically faithful but rejected because the Japanese used `によって` for English `depending on`; the relation guard only recognized `により`. Expanded the generic condition marker to include `によって` and added a regression test using participant compensation/experiment dependence. Quality tests **186/186**, typecheck, and diff check pass. This reduces a measured false reject without weakening checks for missing condition relations; no production cascade default change.

The quality-only recheck artifact `selective-cascade-v604-quality-recheck.json` reclassifies only the Thermal condition row to accepted (**6/10**). The interactive-jewellery row remains rejected/manual-review despite automatic score 1.0 because it retains the untranslated ordinary term `multinationals`; this is documented as a false-accept risk rather than relaxed by rule.

Audit errors now distinguish cascade-only failures such as an untranslated ordinary Latin lexeme or sentence compression from the general quality reasons, without changing production acceptance policy. Focused tests **195/195**, typecheck, and diff check pass.

## v609 technical phrase false-reject reduction (2026-09-26)

The cascade lexeme guard was over-rejecting retained technical phrases when the shorter first word was omitted from the long-token set (`lumped elements`). It now checks contiguous source neighbors using all source/output tokens and exempts a retained multiword phrase while continuing to reject a lone ordinary word such as `precedent`. Added regression coverage; quality tests **187/187**, typecheck and diff check pass. This is cascade-only and does not weaken primary quality acceptance.

### v635 — arXiv metadata overlay no longer breaks abstract paragraph continuation

- Investigation of the ergonomics/iHCI PDF showed the abstract was split into an incomplete body block, an `arXiv:2111.04880[cs.HC] 0` metadata line classified as `paragraph`, and the continuation. The existing transparent-overlay rule only accepted `title` role plus a large font, so this common export variant was not skipped during continuation repair.
- Generalized `isArxivOverlayBlock` to accept a complete arXiv marker emitted as either `title` or `paragraph`, matching the whole marker rather than arbitrary mentions of arXiv. This is format-generic and does not alter ordinary body sentences.
- After reconstruction, the abstract source is again one paragraph spanning the continuation; the metadata marker remains a separate non-translated block.
- `src/test/readingOrder/readingOrder.test.ts`: 73/73 passed. Extraction corpus: all 56 tests passed, but Vitest reported an existing worker `onTaskUpdate` timeout after completion (exit 1); no assertion failed. `npm run typecheck` passed; `npm run lint` passed with four pre-existing warnings; `git diff --check` passed.
- Next: apply the same diagnostic to the medical review continuation rows, then rerun the protection A/B/C benchmark on clean ordinary-body blocks. Do not change production protection until the paired results and manual review are recorded.
### v636 — IEEE Abstract— continuation is reconstructed in the medical review fixture

- The medical imaging review exposed a second generic extraction boundary: a multi-line `Abstract—...` body was classified as `title`, then its lowercase continuation was emitted as a separate paragraph. This was independent of the arXiv overlay case.
- Added a document-generic rule in `mergeColumnContinuations` that recognizes long sentence-like `Abstract—` title blocks as paragraph bodies before continuation resolution, and widened the existing same-column continuation geometry from only `single` columns to matching `left`/`right` columns. It still requires unfinished prose, lowercase continuation, matching x/font, and a tight baseline gap.
- Reconstructed output now contains the full abstract in one paragraph; `Index Terms—...` remains separate. The medical real-paper baseline test passes.
- Validation: targeted extraction baseline 1/1 passed, typecheck passed, diff check passed. Full extraction corpus should be rerun at the next checkpoint because this changes shared block merging.
- Next: rerun the full extraction corpus and then resume the protection A/B/C diagnostic on clean ordinary-body rows; production protection remains unchanged.

- The full extraction command was started after v636 but was manually interrupted after the reading-order suite completed; the baseline half was still CPU-bound and produced no assertion failure before interruption.
- Focused real-paper reading-order checks for `ergonomics-human-factors-ihci` and `medical-imaging-deep-learning-review` pass 2/2. Typecheck and diff check remain clean.
- The widened same-column rule is intentionally constrained by matching column, x/font, baseline gap, unfinished source, and lowercase continuation; it did not alter either focused fixture's expected reading order.

## v760 — protection A/B evidence consolidated (2026-09-26)

- Reviewed the existing same-model, same-greedy protection cohort (`protection-ab-v715-12.json`, 12 manually adjudicated blocks) before changing production protection. Raw, minimal, and current arms all exhibited source-block omissions on several multi-sentence units; the same omission pattern occurred without placeholders, so protection is not the primary cause of those losses. The primary attribution is translation-unit/model behavior, with source-block scope as a secondary factor.
- Current protection did add measurable decode failures on this cohort (4/12), while raw and minimal decoded all 12. Conversely, raw/minimal frequently dropped tracked identifiers/citations because they intentionally exposed them to the model; current restored protected spans when it decoded successfully. This demonstrates a real protection benefit/cost trade-off and does not justify removing protection globally.
- Manual review marked 8/12 rows severity >=2, mostly omissions or semantic shifts shared by all arms. The result is diagnostic, not a product fallback estimate: the cohort contains long or structurally ambiguous blocks and is not a held-out random sample.
- No production protection or routing change was made. Next experiment should separate long multi-sentence source-unit failures from protection effects, use a fresh cross-paper cohort, and report fact-preservation and semantic review per arm rather than treating decode success as quality.

- This change intentionally prioritizes semantic safety for the demonstrated rescue case. It may increase fallback for quote-heavy prose until a safe literal-preservation strategy is evaluated; no blacklist or paper-specific term was added.

### v1010 protection ablation diagnosis (2026-09-28)
- Fixed `translation-server/scripts/diagnose_a_cohort_variants.py` so raw/atomic conditions accept the current restore/protection keyword arguments; prior run had a harness-only TypeError before decode.
- Re-ran `ozchi-author-year` in a fresh MADLAD 3B process with identical greedy settings. Artifact: `translation-server/benchmarks/translation-unit-variants-v79.json`.
- Whole raw input (64 input tokens) translated with full-width citation names/numbers; no hallucinated topic, but citation fidelity is weaker. Current protection and atomic author-year protection (32 input tokens) produced the same semantically correct Japanese and restored the citation exactly.
- This fixture does not show current protection causing semantic drift. It does show protection materially changes tokenization/output formatting and protects citation fidelity. The separate 582-character interactive-jewellery ordinary paragraph still falls back under production quality gate; sentence-level probe showed sentence 1 itself can decode to unrelated content while sentences 2–5 produce Japanese, so length/semicolon splitting alone is insufficient.
- No production behavior changed in v1010; diagnostic-only.

### v1011 multi-domain protection ablation (2026-09-28)
- Replayed three independent clean fallback fixtures in fresh MADLAD 3B processes with the same greedy decode: thermal-earring (ergonomics/biomedical), cognitive-psychology GPT-3 causal reasoning, and linguistics language-model probing.
- Artifacts: `translation-server/benchmarks/translation-unit-variants-v1010-thermal-earring-b-01a329cd.json`, `...-cognitive-psychology-gpt3-b-9c57b65a.json`, `...-linguistics-language-model-physics-b-30cd3318.json`.
- Raw whole-source inputs were rejected as degenerate in all three cases. Current protection also rejected the whole source in all three, but for a distinct reason: protected placeholder drop (`SI Appendix`, `CFG`, or `section 6.1`). This is direct evidence that protection can add reader-visible fallback even when the underlying source is clean.
- Current protection on semantic units was mixed: thermal units 1–2 accepted, unit 0 rejected for `section 6.1`; cognitive units 1 and 3 accepted while units 0 and 2 rejected for `SI Appendix`; linguistics units 1–2 accepted while unit 0 rejected for `BERT`.
- This is diagnostic evidence only. It does not justify removing protection globally: the earlier OzCHI citation fixture showed protection preserving citation fidelity, and raw output changed names/numbers to full-width forms. Next step is a minimal-protection ablation that keeps only opaque spans and leaves ordinary identifiers/context visible, then compare fact preservation and fallback across the same cases.

### v1012–v1013 minimal-protection diagnostic (2026-09-28)
- Added an audit-only `whole_minimal_protection` condition to the variant harness. It exposes readable identifiers and standalone footnote numbers while retaining opaque citation/scientific spans; no production path uses it.
- Initial minimal definition still protected standalone `24` and therefore produced placeholder-drop fallback. After correcting the classifier to expose standalone 1–3 digit markers, the cognitive fixture's minimal whole-source input became `degenerate translation output` rather than placeholder-drop.
- This separates two costs: current protection adds deterministic placeholder-drop fallback; reducing protection removes that specific failure but does not make the long whole-source decode reliable. Semantic-unit segmentation remains necessary for this fixture.
- Artifact: `translation-server/benchmarks/translation-unit-variants-v1013-cognitive-minimal.json`. The harness modifications are diagnostic-only and require a broader cohort before any production policy change.
